# plain-tables

- Dialects: mysql, postgres, sqlite
- Default: off (enable it under `rules` in schemalens.yml)

## Why

Functions, triggers and views are logic and structure that live in the database but not in the model, so ORMs and migration diffs cannot see them and they change behavior behind the application's back.

## Fix

Move the logic into application code, or keep the object and exclude it with a written reason. Options under rules.plain-tables.options: exclude (exact object names), exclude_prefixes (name prefixes, for objects a migration tool creates) and exclude_extensions (true skips PostgreSQL objects owned by an extension).

## Exception

Objects created by an extension or by the migration tool itself, and deliberate database-side logic such as an audit trigger, when the reason is written down.

The same text is printed by `schemalens explain plain-tables`. An exclusion needs a written reason. Back to the [rule index](README.md).
